questions.question: What is "global citizenship"?
options: The idea that all people belong to a single global community with shared responsibilities
A passport issued by the UN
Giving up national citizenship
A type of trade agreement
questions.explanation: Global citizenship is the idea that all people belong to a single global community with responsibilities beyond national borders.

questions.question: Does global citizenship replace national citizenship?
options: No, it adds another layer of identity and responsibility
Yes, it abolishes national citizenship
Yes, it replaces all governments
It has no relation to national citizenship
questions.explanation: Global citizenship does not replace national citizenship — it adds another layer of identity and responsibility.

questions.question: What is "cosmopolitanism"?
options: The idea that all humans belong to a single moral community
A type of national tax
A military alliance
A social media trend
questions.explanation: Cosmopolitanism, rooted in ancient Greek thought, holds that all human beings belong to a single moral community.

questions.question: How has globalisation affected identity, according to the chapter?
options: Many people now feel multiple, overlapping identities
Everyone has exactly one fixed identity
Identity no longer exists
People only identify with their local village
questions.explanation: Globalisation has led many people to feel multiple, overlapping identities through cultural exchange, migration and digital connectivity.

questions.question: What does the phrase "think globally, act locally" capture?
options: You can be a global citizen through meaningful actions in your own community
You must travel the world to make a difference
Local action is pointless
Global problems cannot be addressed
questions.explanation: "Think globally, act locally" captures the idea that meaningful global citizenship often happens through local action.
